newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REDSKINS ROUT DALLAS IN FINAL GAME AT RFK STADIUM.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REDSKINS ROUT DALLAS IN FINAL GAME AT RFK STADIUM.

text.p: The Washington Redskins turned the final game at RFK Stadium into a three-hour farewell party on Sunday as they routed their archrivals, the Dallas Cowboys, 37-10.
Thousands of fans stormed the field after the game. Most grabbed clumps of sod in an attempt to collect souvenirs. One fan was caught on television burning a replica Cowboys' helmet.

At halftime, the Redskins welcomed back dozens of former players, including Sonny Jurgensen, Charley Taylor, John Riggins, Art Monk, Billy Kilmer, Dexter Manley and Bobby Mitchell, as they saluted their fans.
Unfortunately, the game had no playoff ramifications for the Redskins, who were eliminated after last Sunday's 27-26 loss at Arizona.
Redskins owner Jack Kent Cooke signed a deal with Prince George's County, Maryland, last March to move his team into a new stadium scheduled for completion for the start of the 1997 season.
Cooke, who had been threatening for years to move the Redskins out of RFK Stadium in Washington, D.C., invested $360 million of his own money for a new stadium for his team.
The new Redskins stadium will be natural grass and seat 78,600. It will include more than 280 luxury boxes.
